clue.text: Almost no sweat in underwear for country people

indicators.note: one thing set in another is enclosed by it, so the shortened word goes inside

parts.note: pants are underpants in British English

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: 'no sweat' means ease, no difficulty

explanation.surface: Someone shrugging off underwear worries on behalf of rural folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No sweat' is an idiom for something easy, so it stands for a word meaning ease rather than anything to do with perspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Peasants are poor farming folk who live and work on the land, outside towns.

clue.text: Column standard by American editor on the up

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
A is the abbreviation for American

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A newspaper column judged by a rising American editor.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade is a procession of marchers formed up in a long line, which is a column.

clue.text: Everyone old with aches ultimately suffers

parts.note: everyone is all
O is a standard abbreviation for old
W is short for with

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of aches

explanation.surface: Every elderly person with pains endures in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffer something in the old sense is to tolerate or permit it, which is what allows means.

clue.text: Become an expert in pruning minute plant

indicators.note: pruning cuts something away, so a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: to master a subject is to become expert in it
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: Advice to get skilled at cutting back a tiny plant, with pruning a gardening word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' reads as tiny, but it is the M taken out of MASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An aster is a daisy-like flowering garden plant, often called a Michaelmas daisy.

parts.note: 'all the same' means nevertheless, though
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Someone surprised that the temperature has not changed at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy!' looks like an exclamation of surprise, but it is the noun fancy, a notion.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is an idea or notion that comes into the mind, which is a thought.

clue.text: Takes advantage of sailors in steamship

indicators.note: being in a vessel means sitting inside it, so one word is placed within another

parts.note: SS is the prefix for a steamship
a ship's sailors are its crew

explanation.surface: Exploiting the sailors aboard a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw someone is slang for cheating or exploiting them, taking unfair advantage.

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run loose into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone raising adorable wild animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild animals' reads as a phrase, but wild is the signal and animals alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Creatures are living beings, especially animals as distinct from people.

clue.text: Hypnotic state after topless men's arrival

indicators.note: without its top, a word in a down entry loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
a hypnotic state is a trance

explanation.surface: A hypnotist's subject goes under once some bare-chested men turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'has', joining the two parts; topless men are men minus their top letter, not shirtless.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrance is the act of coming in, so it is an arrival on the scene.

clue.text: Husband comes out of shed and rests, awfully agitated

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the remaining letters are jumbled
something that comes out of a word leaves it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
the letters before the husband leaves; 'and' just joins them

explanation.surface: A husband leaves the garden shed and lies down, terribly worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stressed means feeling anxious and tense, which is being agitated.

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
elation is great joy

explanation.surface: A sister jogging along happily.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister is one example of a relative, a family member, as 'maybe' signals.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to outdo or improve on, as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: The capital T suggests the American president; here trump is just the verb to surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: To trump is to surpass or improve on, and a person placing wagers is a bettor or better.

clue.text: Squad leaving area after I object

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: when a letter is leaving a word it departs, so it is struck out

parts.note: a squad is a team
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A squad walks off the field once someone raises an objection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb of protest, but it is the noun, a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single article or thing, which is an object.

parts.note: feeling down is feeling sad
correct means right

explanation.surface: Someone checking whether 'thoroughly sad' is the right description.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright as an adverb means utterly or completely, which is thoroughly.

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the word is read back to front

parts.note: smart means clever

explanation.surface: An exasperated compliment on some ingenious vehicles, flipping used as a mild British oath.
explanation.definitionFit: Trams are passenger vehicles that run on rails laid in the street.

indicators.note: lying in a bed means being inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A fool who has been abandoned in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Clot is British informal for a stupid person, an idiot.

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent into another order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Imagine some racy lap dances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' looks like an imperative verb, but it is the noun, a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a painting or picture of a scene of countryside.

indicators.note: turned means changed around, so these letters take a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether a person has become calmer, and musing on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I wonder' reads as a verb phrase; wonder is the noun, a marvel.
explanation.definitionFit: A miracle is an extraordinary marvel, a wonder.

clue.text: I admit penning half of note in the dark

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so one word holds the other

parts.note: taken as written
to grant a point is to admit it

indicators.note: half of a word keeps only part of it, so the back half is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A confession of writing down part of a note in darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the dark about something is to be uninformed, lacking knowledge of it.

parts.note: a con is a convict; with the 's added
true means faithful, loyal

explanation.surface: Someone grasps that an inmate is faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe words is to interpret their meaning, which is to understand them.

clue.text: Adult's in an excited state after wrong bananas

indicators.note: after places the excited-state piece second, behind the rearranged word
going bananas means going crazy, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
being up means being lively and excited

explanation.surface: A grown person gets worked up after being given the wrong bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like fruit but means crazy; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up is an adult, a person who is fully grown.

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the opening letter of each word counts

parts.note: the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A question about where people sit on bar stools.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pubs are British drinking establishments, the places where people sit on bar stools.

clue.text: Some niff is hardly smelt, perhaps

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the letters are taken from inside the words

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A bit of a pong is barely noticed, with niff British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smelt' reads as the past tense of smell, but a smelt is a small fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The smelt is a small silvery fish, so it is an example of the class, as 'perhaps' signals.

clue.text: Rather like a creamy pudding, half-baked

parts.note: a fool is a dessert of fruit folded into cream
the suffix -ish means rather like or somewhat

explanation.surface: A creamy dessert that has not quite set because it was undercooked.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British pudding of crushed fruit and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-baked idea is poorly thought out, which is foolish.

parts.note: a rat is an informer, someone who tells on others

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: An upset informant regularly spoke to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to unsettle or disconcert them, which is to upset them.

indicators.note: a letter entering a word goes into it, so it is placed inside

parts.note: stats, short for statistics, are data
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A Republican faced with the figures shies away.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to jump or recoil in surprise, which is what someone who flinches does.

clue.text: Starts to obsess about signals in shortwave band

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so each word's first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Someone becomes fixated on the signals in a shortwave radio band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a radio frequency band, but it is a pop group.
explanation.definitionFit: Oasis is the Manchester rock band of the Gallagher brothers, a well-known example of a musical group.

parts.note: broad humour is coarse or vulgar
the cast is the group of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A TV show whose ensemble of actors is crude.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast is a programme sent out on radio or television.

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
EA is the abbreviation for each
M is the abbreviation for month

explanation.surface: A doctor's monthly performance reveals a drive to succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is a cherished aspiration or goal, which is an ambition.

parts.note: taken as written
British roads are graded A for main and B for minor, so this is the B-class kind

explanation.surface: A back road in some foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: British roads are graded A (main) and B (minor), so a minor road is a B ROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Being abroad means being in a foreign country, which is overseas.

clue.text: Boss first to resign after dreadful time in company

indicators.note: after sends the resign piece to the end, behind the dreadful-time-in-company part

parts.note: dire means dreadful

indicators.note: being in a company means being inside it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: first means the opening letter, so only that is taken from the word

parts.note: the first letter of resign

explanation.surface: A boss is the first to quit after a terrible spell in the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' and 'resign' suggest someone quitting a job, but the resignation supplies only a single letter at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: A director sits on a company's board and is one of its bosses.

clue.text: The most wonderful, unfinished ancient city

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
the best is the most wonderful

explanation.surface: Praise for a great ancient city that was never completed.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a famous city of ancient Egypt, and another of ancient Greece.

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
to hamper is to hinder or hold up

explanation.surface: A Tory politician stops a drink from being served.
explanation.walkthrough: Champers is British slang for champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: Champers is informal British for champagne, a sparkling wine and so a drink.
